messages:
maya: FYI customer INC-4532 — their internal ALB target group is 0/3 healthy and our API behind it is returning intermittent 502/503s. They say curl from a bastion to instance works but ALB health checks failing. Error from our proxy: 'upstream connect error or connection timed out'.

josh-netops: Can you share ALB type (internal vs internet), target type (instance/ip), health check config and the instance SG rules? Might be SGs blocking ALB nodes.

maya: Internal ALB, target type: instance. Health check: HTTP /healthz port 8080 interval 10 timeout 5 unhealthy 2. ALB SG: sg-0a1b2c3d. Instance SG: sg-0f9e8d7c. Instance SG ingress currently: tcp 8080 from 10.10.10.0/24 (monitoring) and our office static IPs. NACLs are permissive.

anita-engr: Classic SG mistake — if the instance SG allows only CIDRs it won’t accept traffic from the ALB unless the ALB IPs/CIDRs are also allowed. Best practice: allow traffic from the ALB security group (reference the ALB SG as the source).

maya: Confirmed: instance SG has no rule referencing sg-0a1b2c3d. Customer had a strict allowlist and missed the ALB SG. They did run a quick curl from bastion to instance: `curl -sS http://10.0.12.45:8080/healthz` -> `200 OK`. But ALB logs show `target timed out` and VPC flow logs show connections from ALB nodes being rejected.

josh-netops: Can you collect the following and share? `aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn <tg-arn>` and `aws ec2 describe-security-groups --group-ids sg-0a1b2c3d sg-0f9e8d7c`. Also check ELB stickiness? Unrelated but useful.

maya: Pasted outputs (redacted): target-health -> "unhealthy (connection timed out)"; SG describe shows instance SG ingress only 10.10.10.0/24 and office IPs, no SG refs.

anita-engr: Quick remediation: add inbound rule to instance SG to allow tcp/8080 from source sg-0a1b2c3d. Example CLI: `aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-0f9e8d7c --protocol tcp --port 8080 --source-group sg-0a1b2c3d` — do it in staging first. That will let ALB health checks reach the instance without opening to broad CIDRs.

lucy-cs: Can you write a 1-2 line customer-facing summary explaining root cause and fix so I can update the ticket?

maya: Summary for customer: "Root cause: instance security group was locked to a CIDR allowlist and did not permit traffic from the ALB nodes. ALB health checks originate from the ALB SG; because the instance SG did not reference the ALB SG, health checks timed out. Fix: add a security-group-based inbound rule to allow the ALB SG to connect to port 8080. We verified by updating the SG in staging and observing target group drift to healthy; will apply in prod during the change window."

josh-netops: Also a few follow-ups — (1) check for any custom NACLs that might drop ephemeral ports from the ALB, (2) confirm target type: if they switch to ip targets the same SG logic still applies but with ENI IPs, (3) consider health check path TTL/caching only if DNS involved.

platform-bot: reminder: run `aws elbv2 describe-target-health` after change and check CloudWatch metric `UnhealthyHostCount`.

maya: We requested permission to change SG in prod outside hours, customer approved for a quick patch. Applied rule in prod: `aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-0f9e8d7c --protocol tcp --port 8080 --source-group sg-0a1b2c3d` at 1792107600.

josh-netops: Confirmed target group -> 3/3 healthy within 30s of SG change. VPC flow logs show ACCEPT from ALB node IPs now.

maya: Customer re-tested API flows — errors dropped to 0 and latency normalized. Closing INC-4532. Thanks all :thumbsup:

lucy-cs: Filing quick KB note so CS can reference in future: "Internal ALB health checks failing when instance SG uses CIDR-only allowlist — recommend SG-to-SG rule."

anita-engr: One more note for engineering docs — add a checklist item for private ALB onboarding: verify instance SG allows ALB SG, check health check protocol/port, and confirm path returns 200 without redirect.

maya: Marking resolved, will attach ELB logs and the SG diff to the ticket.
